recent_posts.title: How the changing software industry is impacting junior developers
recent_posts.summary: Justin Searls appeared on the freeCodeCamp podcast with Quincy Larson to discuss how the rapidly changing software industry is affecting junior developers and what they can do about it. Searls, who started programming in the 90s, acknowledges he can't fully relate to the current experience of newcomers. He has historically discouraged people from entering software development unless truly passionate, a stance at odds with the 'learn to code' movement that has recently hit significant headwinds. The episode is ~90 minutes long and available on YouTube and as a podcast.

recent_posts.title: Why AI agents signal we are not in a bubble
recent_posts.summary: Ben Thompson argues that AI is not in a bubble, primarily because of the emergence of functional AI agents. He traces three LLM inflection points: ChatGPT (2022), OpenAI's o1 reasoning model (2024), and agentic systems like Claude Code and Codex (late 2025). Agents address most of ChatGPT's original flaws by verifying their own outputs without human involvement. Crucially, agents reduce the number of people needed to drive massive compute demand, since one person can direct multiple agents. On the enterprise side, companies are economically incentivized to replace human organizational overhead with agents, fueling sustained capex investment. Thompson also argues that the model-plus-harness integration required for effective agents undermines the commodity-model thesis, positioning Anthropic and OpenAI as durable value-chain integrators. Microsoft's Copilot Cowork, built on Anthropic's Claude rather than a model-agnostic stack, is cited as evidence that compelling agentic products require tight model-harness integration.

recent_posts.title: Dual-loop BDD is the new Red-green TDD
recent_posts.summary: Justin Searls shares how he upgraded his AI coding agent (Claude Code) from simple red-green TDD to the dual-loop BDD approach. Simple red-green TDD caused agents to chase code coverage with unit tests while missing real integration correctness. The dual-loop approach starts each feature with a failing integration test (outer loop), drives implementation through unit-level red-green-refactor cycles (inner loop), then returns to verify the integration test passes. He provides a ready-to-use prompt for AGENTS.md files. He also notes with some irony that many developers who previously rejected TDD are now embracing it—not to validate their own code, but to verify AI-generated code.

recent_posts.title: Claude's macOS Electron app is buggy enough to uninstall
recent_posts.summary: A developer criticizes Anthropic's Claude desktop app for macOS, calling it a buggy Electron app, and has uninstalled it in favor of using it in a Safari tab. The post contrasts this with ChatGPT's native macOS app, which works more reliably, and links to a blog post lamenting the decline of native app development.

recent_posts.title: Claude Cowork causes Mac system unresponsiveness due to 10GB VM bundle
recent_posts.summary: Claude Cowork, a multi-agent coding feature in Claude Code, causes severe Mac performance degradation after a few minutes of use. The system becomes entirely unresponsive, traced to a GitHub issue showing the Cowork feature creates a 10GB VM bundle that tanks system performance.

recent_posts.title: How AI coding agents are eroding collaborative software development
recent_posts.summary: AI coding agents are driving a shift toward what the author calls 'Antisocial Coding' — a trend away from collaborative, social development practices. Three key observations: agents create hub-and-spoke communication bottlenecks that make multi-developer collaboration unwieldy; agent-built codebases calcify quickly into overly complex, single-owner projects; and open source projects are closing off contributions (e.g., tldraw removing its test suite to prevent agent-assisted rewrites). The downstream effects include increased bus-factor risk, erosion of collective code ownership, and fewer mentorship opportunities for junior developers. Engineering leaders are urged to consider these organizational impacts before optimizing purely for agent productivity.

recent_posts.title: My coding agent harnesses are designed…
recent_posts.summary: Justin Searls describes his approach to running multiple AI coding agents in parallel tabs, all committing directly to main rather than using git worktrees. His tool turbocommit supports this workflow by linking commits across sessions, preserving every prompt and protecting progress when using Claude Code.

recent_posts.title: The Cart of Theseus when every Instacart item gets substituted
recent_posts.summary: A witty riff on the Ship of Theseus thought experiment applied to Instacart grocery orders: when every item in your order gets substituted, is it still your order? The author argues it isn't, while Instacart customer support disagrees.

recent_posts.title: AI agents have made the 10x developer debate irrelevant
recent_posts.summary: Justin Searls references a 2023 prediction he made about the demise of the '10x developer' concept, arguing that AI agents have rendered the decades-long debate moot by effectively equalizing or amplifying developer output across the board.

recent_posts.title: Why there is no playbook to make yourself irreplaceable from AI
recent_posts.summary: A sharp, one-paragraph hot take responding to reader feedback about AI job displacement: if there were a reliable process to make yourself irreplaceable, AI agents would simply follow that same process and replace you anyway.

top_posts.title: Test-driven development skills are essential for working with AI coding agents
top_posts.summary: Test-driven development skills are becoming critical for working effectively with AI coding agents. Developers experienced in TDD are both the most skeptical of AI code generation and the most successful at using it, because they understand how to build verification into workflows. AI agents, like human developers, need independent ways to verify their work—without verification, they resort to guessing, which compounds errors rapidly. The ability to establish automated testing and verification mechanisms, once a hallmark of agile practices, is now essential for enabling AI agents to produce reliable code through reinforcement learning.

top_posts.title: What happens to white collar workers if AI investments actually pay off
top_posts.summary: A developer's blunt take on the economic consequences if AI investments actually pay off. The author argues that tech CEOs are being dishonest about job creation, that white-collar workers in accounting, law, and consulting face severe displacement, and that programmers will remain busy but spread thinner across more projects. The post warns of 'The Fuckening'—a macroeconomically significant collapse in high-paying office jobs—and offers individualized survival advice: quantify your direct contribution to revenue, position yourself close to the money, and continuously reassess your value as AI tools improve.

top_posts.title: Apple's scheduled iMessage fails across time zones
top_posts.summary: A scheduled iMessage failed to send due to a timezone-related bug in Apple's implementation. When crossing time zones, the scheduled send time (10 AM) never occurred locally, causing the message to remain permanently unsent instead of being based on an absolute timestamp.

top_posts.title: iMessage treats phone numbers with country codes as separate contacts
top_posts.summary: iMessage continues to treat phone numbers with and without country codes (+1) as separate contacts while grouping them in the same message thread, creating a frustrating user experience that forces users to potentially save duplicate contact entries for US phone numbers.
